nodes.label: The Last Human-Written Paper: Agent-Native Research Artifacts
nodes.author: Liu et al.

nodes.label: Storytelling Tax
nodes.rationale: The systematic erasure of research process knowledge imposed by compilation into narrative form; research branches and backtracks but publication flattens this into linear story, discarding failed experiments and rejected hypotheses

nodes.label: Engineering Tax
nodes.rationale: The gap between reviewer-sufficient documentation (what convinces humans) and agent-sufficient documentation (what enables correct execution); tacit knowledge exists in no written document

nodes.label: Agent-Native Research Artifact (ARA) Protocol
nodes.rationale: Recasts primary research object from narrative document to agent-executable knowledge package organized into four interlocking layers: structured scientific logic, executable code with full specifications, exploration graph preserving branching process, and grounded evidence

nodes.label: Live Research Manager
nodes.rationale: Mechanism that captures research decisions and dead ends as natural side-effects of everyday development, producing conforming ARA artifacts without additional documentation burden

nodes.label: ARA Compiler
nodes.rationale: Translates legacy PDFs, repositories, and supplementary materials into ARA format, providing backward compatibility with existing publication ecosystem

nodes.label: ARA-Native Review System
nodes.rationale: Automates structural verification and budget-aware reproduction (analogous to grammar checker for prose), redirecting expert attention from mechanical checking to judgment

nodes.label: Exploration Graph
nodes.rationale: Preserves branching research process including failed experiments, rejected hypotheses, and design pivots; structured as decision DAG with dead-end nodes marking failure modes

nodes.label: Forensic Bindings
nodes.rationale: Cross-layer links connecting claims in /logic to evidence in /evidence and code in /src, enabling agents to trace reasoning from abstract claims to concrete implementations and empirical results

nodes.label: Knowledge over Narrative Principle
nodes.rationale: Core design principle of ARA: organized, evolving knowledge produced during research is the primary scientific object; narrative paper is a compiled view

nodes.label: Progressive Disclosure
nodes.rationale: ARA structure supports loading only layers and files relevant to agent's current task, avoiding unnecessary context pollution in finite context windows

nodes.label: Agent-Native Research Artifact (ARA) Protocol
nodes.rationale: Structured format for research knowledge with four layers (Cognitive, Physical, Exploration Graph, Evidence) designed to enable agent understanding, reproduction, learning, and verification of research contributions.

nodes.label: Cognitive Layer (/logic)
nodes.rationale: Contains what was done and why: problem definition, solution architecture, falsifiable claims with proof pointers, and verification plans. Replaces passive citations with typed dependencies (imports, bounds, baselines).

nodes.label: Physical Layer (/src)
nodes.rationale: Contains executable code calibrated to contribution type. Algorithmic contributions use kernel mode (core modules only); systemic contributions use repository mode (full implementation with index mapping).

nodes.label: Exploration Graph (/trace)
nodes.rationale: Stores complete research DAG as nested YAML with five typed node kinds (question, decision, experiment, dead_end, pivot). Functions as 'git log for research', preserving hypotheses and failure modes that narrative papers discard.

nodes.label: Evidence Layer (/evidence)
nodes.rationale: Contains raw outputs grounding every claim: machine-readable metric tables, generated data with exact values and source annotations, training curves, resource usage, and diagnostics. Enables layered access control by separating logic from data.

nodes.label: Live Research Manager
nodes.rationale: Background system that distills researcher-agent conversations into typed events accumulating across ARA layers. Three-stage pipeline: Context Harvester → Event Router → Maturity Tracker. Enables zero-documentation-overhead artifact population.

nodes.label: Context Harvester
nodes.rationale: Scans session record (conversational history, tool outputs, experiment results, code diffs) to extract research-significant events: actions AI agent performed and directions researcher expressed or confirmed.

nodes.label: Event Router
nodes.rationale: Classifies extracted events into seven types (decision, experiment, dead_end, pivot, claim, heuristic, observation), tags with provenance (user, ai-suggested, ai-executed, user-revised), and routes to appropriate ARA layer.

nodes.label: Maturity Tracker
nodes.rationale: Reviews staging area and promotes observations with sufficient evidence into formal entries. Crystallizes at two timescales: continuously appends trace events; periodically crystallizes into structured layers when closure signals indicate settlement.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler
nodes.rationale: Agent skill that translates legacy research sources (PDFs, code repos, datasets, rubrics, trajectory logs) into complete ARAs. Performs forensic reconstruction to recover cross-layer lineage from implicit sources.

nodes.label: Semantic Deconstruction
nodes.rationale: First stage of top-down ARA generation: strips narrative framing to expose raw research content (formulations, configurations, results, dependencies, failed approaches) in fact-dense telegraphic form.

nodes.label: Cognitive Mapping
nodes.rationale: Second stage: populates /logic with motivation chain, falsifiable claims with proof pointers, formal concepts, and solution structure, with every claim linked to verifying experiment.

nodes.label: Physical Grounding
nodes.rationale: Third stage: generates /src with annotated configurations, typed code stubs, and environment manifest. When code repository available, performs code-paper reconciliation to surface tacit knowledge.

nodes.label: Exploration Graph Extraction
nodes.rationale: Fourth stage: reconstructs research DAG as nested YAML tree with dead-end leaf nodes documenting hypothesis, failure mode, and lesson.

nodes.label: ARA Seal
nodes.rationale: Three-level machine-verifiable credential: Level 1 (Structural Integrity, seconds), Level 2 (Argumentative Rigor, minutes), Level 3 (Execution Reproducibility, hours-days). Passes issue Seal Certificate for downstream verification.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 1: Structural Integrity
nodes.rationale: Verifies artifact is well-formed and internally consistent: directory ontology exists, structured files conform to schema, all cross-layer references resolve.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 2: Argumentative Rigor
nodes.rationale: Rigor Auditor agent evaluates epistemically sound content along six objective dimensions: evidence relevance, falsifiability quality, methodological rigor, scope calibration, argument coherence, exploration integrity. Scored 1-5 per dimension.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 3: Execution Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Verifies central claims reproduce empirically via scaled-down directional checks. Verifying agent isolated from evidence layer (receives only code kernel and algorithm descriptions) to prevent fabrication.

nodes.label: Rigor Auditor Agent
nodes.rationale: Agent skill that executes ARA Seal Level 2 without executing code or consulting external sources. Evaluates epistemically sound content along six objective dimensions with anchored rubrics.

nodes.label: Three-Stage ARA Review Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Mirrors CI/CD practices: Stage 1 (Conceptual Verification, minutes) checks structural integrity and argumentative rigor; Stage 2 (Empirical Verification, hours-days) tests claim reproducibility; Stage 3 (Human Review, days-weeks) focuses on significance, novelty, taste.

nodes.label: CI Report
nodes.rationale: Output of Stage 1 (Conceptual Verification): records structural failures, rigor critiques, and advisory diagnostics (dead-end nodes, baseline coverage, experiment-claim gaps).

nodes.label: Empirical Review Report
nodes.rationale: Output of Stage 2 (Empirical Verification): records which claims verified, which failed, which deferred due to budget, and experimental gaps identified.

nodes.label: (Human+AI)² Research Network
nodes.rationale: Scientific communication system where ARA is primary object. Researchers pursue questions; paper accrues automatically as ARA. Agents render on demand into surfaces needed. Contributions compound at artifact level; publishing becomes Git-like operation.

nodes.label: PAPER.md Manifest
nodes.rationale: Root manifest with YAML frontmatter and layer index enabling agent to triage relevance in ~500 tokens. Enables efficient navigation of ARA structure.

nodes.label: Typed Dependencies in Related Work
nodes.rationale: Replaces passive citations with machine-executable dependency graph: imports inject prior definitions, bounds propagate constraints to hyperparameter search, baseline entries enable automatic regression detection.

nodes.label: Kernel Mode (Algorithmic Contributions)
nodes.rationale: For algorithmic contributions: only core modules with typed I/O signatures, often 1-2 orders of magnitude smaller than full repository, enabling coding agents to regenerate environment-native boilerplate on demand.

nodes.label: Repository Mode (Systemic Contributions)
nodes.rationale: For systemic contributions (CUDA kernels, distributed training, systems architectures): full implementation retained but annotated via index.md manifest mapping each source file to ARA component.

nodes.label: Configs Annotation
nodes.rationale: Every hyperparameter annotated with rationale and search range in configs/ directory, enabling agents to understand design choices and parameter sensitivity.

nodes.label: Environment Manifest
nodes.rationale: Pins dependencies, hardware, and seeds with mode specification, forensic bindings, and detailed rationale enabling reproducible execution.

nodes.label: problem.md
nodes.rationale: Defines the gap and key insight in the research contribution.

nodes.label: solution/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Specifies architecture, algorithm, and convergence-critical heuristics.

nodes.label: claims.md
nodes.rationale: Distills falsifiable assertions with explicit proof pointers to experiments and evidence.

nodes.label: experiments.md
nodes.rationale: Declares the verification plan for all claims.

nodes.label: related_work.md
nodes.rationale: Contains typed dependencies replacing passive citations, enabling machine-executable dependency graph.

nodes.label: results/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Contains machine-readable metric tables and generated data with exact values and source annotations.

nodes.label: logs/ Directory
nodes.rationale: Captures training curves, resource usage, and diagnostics.

nodes.label: AI-Native Research Paradigm
nodes.rationale: Research increasingly conducted through collaboration between researcher and general-purpose coding agent across full lifecycle. Process born digital and textual, enabling comprehensive research-process capture at negligible marginal cost.

nodes.label: Design Principle P1: Silent, Framework-Independent Integration
nodes.rationale: Live Research Manager is natural-language specification loadable by any coding agent, requiring no custom SDKs. Runs as background process collecting traces without researcher intervention.

nodes.label: Design Principle P2: Faithful Epistemic Provenance
nodes.rationale: Every event tagged with provenance (user, ai-suggested, ai-executed, user-revised). Raw observations staged rather than forced into categories, maturing progressively as evidence accumulates.

nodes.label: Design Principle P3: Comprehensive Trajectory Capture
nodes.rationale: Full branching research process including dead ends and pivots recorded with cross-layer bindings. Version-controlled so each milestone produces navigable snapshot; retroactive revisions are first-class operations.

nodes.label: Seven Research Event Types
nodes.rationale: Decision, experiment, dead_end, pivot, claim, heuristic, observation. Each carries structured payload enabling machine-executable research record.

nodes.label: Progressive Crystallization
nodes.rationale: Two-timescale artifact construction: continuously appends trace events at session boundaries; periodically crystallizes observations into structured layers when closure signals indicate settlement.

nodes.label: Closure Signals
nodes.rationale: Indicators that observation has been treated as settled: topic abandonment, explicit researcher affirmation, empirical resolution of linked experiments, or artifact-level commitment.

nodes.label: Session Record
nodes.rationale: Short record written at session close: events captured, claims touched, open threads. Appended to running session index for cross-session continuity.

nodes.label: Universal Input, Canonical Output Principle
nodes.rationale: ARA Compiler is many-to-one: accepts any combination of PDFs, code repos, datasets, rubrics, trajectory logs; always produces single ARA conforming to protocol. Degradation graceful.

nodes.label: High-Fidelity Preservation Principle
nodes.rationale: Every numerical result, hyperparameter, architectural detail, and negative finding in sources must appear somewhere in artifact. Missing PDF-accessible information constitutes compilation failure.

nodes.label: Knowledge Lineage Principle
nodes.rationale: Compiler performs forensic reconstruction recovering cross-layer forensic bindings from sources where lineage exists only implicitly, enabling agents to trace claims downstream to code or upstream to hypotheses.

nodes.label: Forensic Reconstruction
nodes.rationale: Process of recovering cross-layer forensic bindings connecting claims to experiments, experiments to evidence, and evidence to code from sources where lineage exists only implicitly.

nodes.label: Code-Paper Reconciliation
nodes.rationale: Cross-referencing codebase against claims to surface tacit knowledge: implicit assumptions, undocumented tricks, extra parameters. Written back to /logic as provenance-tagged heuristics.

nodes.label: Collective Inference
nodes.rationale: When library of previously compiled ARAs available, Compiler retrieves heuristics and configurations from same-domain artifacts, flags common patterns current paper omits, adds as candidate heuristics tagged collective_inference.

nodes.label: Design Principle P1: Automate Mechanical, Reserve Humans for Judgment
nodes.rationale: Structural validity, internal consistency, and claim reproducibility are objective properties; significance, novelty, and taste require domain expertise. Never ask human to verify machine-checkable issues.

nodes.label: Design Principle P2: Reproducibility as Foundational Requirement
nodes.rationale: Reproducibility is machine-verified property of artifact itself. Passing Level 1 is submission requirement; Level 2 produces critique before compute spent on Level 3; results attached to every review.

nodes.label: Seal Certificate
nodes.rationale: Signed record of artifact ID, verification level achieved, timestamp, environment hash, and per-claim reproduction outcomes. Downstream agents check before investing compute.

nodes.label: Stage 1: Conceptual Verification
nodes.rationale: Checks whether artifact is well-formed and conceptually well-supported without running experiments. Validates structural integrity (Level 1) and argumentative rigor (Level 2). Produces CI Report.

nodes.label: Stage 2: Empirical Verification
nodes.rationale: Tests whether claimed results reproduce. Executes ARA Seal Level 3 with venue-specified compute budget. Agent isolated from evidence layer. Produces Empirical Review Report.

nodes.label: Stage 3: Human Review
nodes.rationale: Human reviewers focus on judgment questions: significance, novelty, taste, ethical implications. Receive submission with CI Report and Empirical Review Report. Write structured reviews linked to ARA components.

nodes.label: PaperBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 23 peer-reviewed ML papers with 8,921 expert-authored rubric requirements. Supplies configuration depth via expert rubrics encoding hyperparameters, implementation tricks, configurations absent from papers.

nodes.label: RE-Bench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 7 R&D hill-climbing tasks with 24,008 agent runs and 46,303 failure episodes. Supplies trajectory depth via METR MALT transcripts with full successful and failure trajectories.

nodes.label: Configuration Depth Gap
nodes.rationale: Across PaperBench's 8,921 expert reproduction requirements, only 45.4% fully specified in source PDF. Published papers omit hyperparameters, environment specs, implementation details necessary for reproduction.

nodes.label: Exploration Depth Gap
nodes.rationale: Across 24,008 RE-Bench agent runs, 90.2% of dollar cost spent on failed exploration discarded from published artifact. Forces each subsequent agent to rediscover same dead ends.

nodes.label: Knowledge Extraction Evaluation (§7.2)
nodes.rationale: Tests what agent can extract from each format. 450 questions across 30 targets in three categories: Category A (surface results), Category B (configuration recovery), Category C (failure knowledge).

nodes.label: Category A: Fidelity
nodes.rationale: Tests fidelity on surface results, methods, conditions answerable from PDF. ARA wins +14.8% while consuming 12% fewer tokens via PAPER.md layer index enabling targeted lookup.

nodes.label: Category B: Configuration Detail
nodes.rationale: Tests configuration recovery on hyperparameters, environment specs, preprocessing details. ARA wins +24.8% via src/configs/ centralizing knowledge papers systematically omit.

nodes.label: Category C: Failure Knowledge
nodes.rationale: Tests failure knowledge on dead ends, alternatives, lessons. ARA wins +65.7% as baseline has no source for failure knowledge; answer lives only in MALT trajectories.

nodes.label: Reproduction Evaluation (§7.3)
nodes.rationale: Tests whether structured artifacts translate understanding into action. 15 PaperBench papers with 10 reproduction tasks each (150 tasks, 1,743 rubric requirements), stratified by difficulty.

nodes.label: Difficulty-Weighted Success Rate Metric
nodes.rationale: Primary metric weighting easy, medium, hard subtasks at 1:2:3 to emphasize harder tasks where structured information provides most leverage.

nodes.label: Extension Evaluation (§7.4)
nodes.rationale: Tests whether agents build on prior work more efficiently with failure knowledge. Uses RE-Bench MALT trajectories to measure whether dead-end knowledge accelerates new research.

nodes.label: ARA Protocol and Format
nodes.rationale: Machine-actionable research artifact format that structures scientific knowledge into four layers (Cognitive, Physical, Exploration, Evidence) with cross-layer bindings to enable agent-native research communication and reproducibility verification.

nodes.label: RE-Bench Extension Experiment
nodes.rationale: Tests whether preserving failure trajectories from prior research enables next agent to extend work more effectively; uses 5 RE-Bench tasks with real MALT agent failure traces to measure whether structured dead-end documentation closes exploration gaps.

nodes.label: Seal Review Protocol
nodes.rationale: Three-level automated review system for ARAs: Level 1 (structural integrity), Level 2 (Rigor Auditor for argumentative rigor), Level 3 (execution reproducibility). Operationalizes auditing across provenance, soundness, claim decomposition, and cryptographic lineage.

nodes.label: Rigor Auditor Component
nodes.rationale: Claude Code SDK agent that reads ARA, builds cross-layer maps, scores six dimensions, and compiles findings list. Detects fabricated claims, rebutted-branch leaks, over-claims, and missing falsifications with 82.6% overall detection rate on mutation benchmark.

nodes.label: Exploration Graph and Dead-End Tracking
nodes.rationale: Promotes dead ends to first-class nodes with structured failure modes and claim cross-references, making negative knowledge machine-queryable. Addresses finding that 59.2% of agent tokens on RE-Bench spent on dead-end exploration discarded by published artifacts.

nodes.label: Cognitive Layer (claims, logic, concepts)
nodes.rationale: Structured scientific logic layer containing claims.md, algorithm.md, concepts.md, and heuristics.md. Encodes claims with explicit Falsification criteria, mathematical formulations, and implementation tricks that PDFs leave implicit or scattered.

nodes.label: Physical Layer (src/ with kernel/repo modes)
nodes.rationale: Executable code layer with two modes: kernel (algorithmic contributions, minimal core modules) and repository (systemic contributions, full implementation with forensic bindings to claims). Provides executable evidence scaled to contribution type.

nodes.label: Evidence Layer (experiments, results, tables)
nodes.rationale: Grounded evidence including experiments.md (combinatorial experiment matrix, evaluation protocols, metrics), results tables, and MALT attempt logs. Makes experiment matrix explicit and machine-enumerable rather than compressed in prose.

nodes.label: Taxonomy of Reproduction-Critical Information
nodes.rationale: Ten-category taxonomy derived from PaperBench rubrics (3,050 leaf requirements): combinatorial experiment matrix (24.1%), evaluation protocol (18.5%), hyperparameters (17.2%), metric logging (10.4%), result interpretation (8.6%), architecture (5.8%), mathematical formulation (4.5%), implementation tricks (4.2%), data pipeline (3.8%), environment/infrastructure (2.9%). Reveals that hyperparameters alone insufficient; combinatorial explosion is dominant challenge.

nodes.label: PaperBench Benchmark
nodes.rationale: 23-paper ML benchmark with expert-authored rubrics decomposing papers into atomic leaf requirements. Used to validate ARA's dimensional coverage and measure agent reproduction success rates (95.6% Cat. A accuracy on Understanding experiment).

nodes.label: Live Research Manager
nodes.rationale: Records research trajectories as work unfolds in AI-native workflows. Closes fidelity ceiling by capturing experimental details, environment specs, and ablation results that PDFs omit. Enables self-maintaining ecosystems where consumption becomes maintenance.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler (PDF to ARA extraction)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code SDK agent that extracts structured ARA from finished PDF papers. Faithfully represents only what PDF contains; wrapped in RE-Bench-specific pipeline for failure-trace layer population from MALT transcripts.

nodes.label: Beat-Reference Filter (fairness mechanism)
nodes.rationale: Direction-aware filter excluding MALT scoring attempts exceeding reference solution, applied per attempt rather than per run. Central fairness rule ensuring neither paper agent nor ARA agent carries worked-out beating-reference solution that could be transcribed.

nodes.label: Claude Sonnet 4.6 Agent Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Comparison of paper agent vs ARA agent on 5 RE-Bench tasks. ARA agent reaches useful first move earlier on all tasks; ends with better score on rust_codecontests, nanogpt_chat_rl, fix_embedding; paper agent overtakes on triton_cumsum and restricted_mlm via moves trace does not name.

nodes.label: Sonnet 4.5 Base Model Inversion
nodes.rationale: On triton_cumsum and restricted_mlm, Sonnet 4.5 trajectories invert Sonnet 4.6 results: ARA agent outperforms paper agent. Suggests artifact value scales with gap between documented trace and agent's own discovery bandwidth; weaker base benefits from ranked heuristic list.

nodes.label: Machine-Readable Science Movement
nodes.rationale: Growing line of work (FAIR principles, W3C PROV, nanopublications, RO-Crate, Whole Tale, Discovery Engine) arguing scientific knowledge should be authored in machine-readable form during research rather than recovered post-hoc. ARA extends this by jointly binding logic, executable code, and decision history with machine-verifiable reproducibility.

nodes.label: Dimensional Gap of Existing Tools
nodes.rationale: Analysis showing PDF, GitHub, and experiment trackers (MLflow, W&B) simultaneously leave knowledge siloed in three unlinked formats with no cross-referencing between claims, code, evidence, and decisions. ARA closes gap by providing executable epistemic graph with cross-layer bindings.

nodes.label: Negative Knowledge and Failed Trajectories
nodes.rationale: Recent work shows failure traces become actionable only when annotated with root-cause structure. Large-scale experiment logs retain >99.99% more search history than papers report. ARA promotes dead ends to first-class nodes, making negative knowledge machine-queryable rather than lost to narrative selection.

nodes.label: Agent-Oriented Documentation and Tooling
nodes.rationale: Convergent body of work showing agents benefit from structured, layered representations over flat corpora. Strongest LLMs implement <40% of novel contributions correctly; semantic misalignment is dominant failure mode. ARA encodes claims, evidence, heuristics, and executable bindings at authoring time, eliminating post-hoc recovery.

nodes.label: Artifact Lineage and Self-Maintaining Ecosystems
nodes.rationale: Near-term extension where each ARA declares parent artifacts and expresses contribution as structured diff. Reduces construction and verification cost; enables self-maintaining ecosystems where consumption becomes maintenance and corrections propagate upstream.

nodes.label: Knowledge Graph and Collaborative Discovery
nodes.rationale: Medium-term extension where aggregated lineages form queryable scientific knowledge graph. Cross-artifact claim alignment turns literature synthesis into subgraph queries; enables continuous review where claim-confidence surface rises with replications and falls with counter-evidence.

nodes.label: Evaluation Scope Limitation (ML-only)
nodes.rationale: Study covers only ML papers where computational reproducibility and well-defined contribution types make ARA's four-layer structure natural fit. Generalization to experimental sciences with physical execution or theoretical disciplines with proof-based results remains empirically untested.

nodes.label: Fidelity Ceiling Limitation
nodes.rationale: ARA fidelity bounded by source of supervision. Compiler faithfully represents only what PDF contains; when paper omits experimental details, environment specs, or ablation results, no extraction method recovers them. Live Research Manager closes gap but assumes AI-native workflow.

nodes.label: Deployment Prerequisites (adversarial robustness, schema evolution)
nodes.rationale: Two properties required for production use not yet implemented: adversarial robustness and privacy guarantees (lack sandboxed execution, content-level anomaly detection, granular access control); schema evolution story for major revisions (versioning, automatic rewriting, deprecation policy).

nodes.label: RE-Bench (Wijk et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Wijk et al.
nodes.rationale: Benchmark with 7 tasks, each with continuously valued automated scorer and METR MALT transcripts containing thousands of complete agent runs with dead ends. Used to test whether structured failure-trace layer enables next agent to extend work more effectively.

nodes.label: PaperBench (Starace et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Starace et al.
nodes.rationale: 42-paper ML benchmark evaluating AI agents on full paper reproduction. Expert-authored rubrics decompose papers into 8,921 atomic leaf requirements across 10 information categories. Provides ground truth for reproduction-critical information taxonomy.

nodes.label: FAIR Principles (Wilkinson et al., 2016)
nodes.author: Wilkinson et al.
nodes.rationale: Standardizes data metadata for scientific knowledge. Part of machine-readable science movement that ARA extends by adding executable semantics and decision history.

nodes.label: W3C PROV Ontology (Lebo et al., 2013)
nodes.author: Lebo et al.
nodes.rationale: Formalizes provenance for scientific outputs. ARA operationalizes provenance through cross-layer bindings and source tags on exploration nodes.

nodes.label: Nanopublications (Groth et al., 2010)
nodes.author: Groth et al.
nodes.rationale: Atomizes claims with provenance. ARA extends by adding execution semantics and decision history not present in nanopublications.

nodes.label: RO-Crate (Soiland-Reyes et al., 2022)
nodes.author: Soiland-Reyes et al.
nodes.rationale: Bundles research objects. ARA provides execution semantics and claim-evidence bindings that RO-Crate lacks.

nodes.label: Whole Tale (Brinckman et al., 2019)
nodes.author: Brinckman et al.
nodes.rationale: Packages computational environments. ARA extends by adding structured logic layer and decision history.

nodes.label: Discovery Engine (Baulin et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Baulin et al.
nodes.rationale: Distills publications into Conceptual Tensor. Unlike ARA, lacks execution semantics and decision history capture.

nodes.label: Reproducibility Crisis in ML (Baker, 2016)
nodes.author: Baker
nodes.rationale: Documents widespread reproducibility failures in ML. Motivates ARA's design to address structural failures of PDF format through machine-actionable artifacts.

nodes.label: EXP-Bench (Kon et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Kon et al.
nodes.rationale: Reports only 0.5% end-to-end experiment success despite 20-35% component accuracy. Demonstrates frontier agents cannot recover knowledge PDFs leave implicit, motivating ARA's structured approach.

nodes.label: Scientific Claim Verification (Wadden et al., 2020)
nodes.author: Wadden et al.
nodes.rationale: Addresses claim verification in scientific papers. ARA operationalizes verification through Seal protocol's three-level review system.

nodes.label: Paper-Code Discrepancy Detection (Baumgärtner & Gurevych, 2026)
nodes.author: Baumgärtner & Gurevych
nodes.rationale: LLMs detect fewer than 46% of paper-code discrepancies. ARA addresses this through explicit cross-layer bindings and forensic code-to-claim mappings.

nodes.label: Failure Trace Annotation (Zhu et al., 2025)
nodes.author: Zhu et al.
nodes.rationale: Shows failure traces become actionable only when annotated with root-cause structure. ARA's exploration graph provides this structure for dead ends.

nodes.label: LLM-as-Judge Pathologies (Zheng et al., 2023)
nodes.author: Zheng et al.
nodes.rationale: Documents grade inflation and finding-score decoupling in LLM evaluation. Rigor Auditor exhibits these pathologies; suggests LLMs should generate findings rather than grades with deterministic verdict computation.

nodes.label: Semantic Misalignment in Code Implementation (Jimenez et al., 2024)
nodes.author: Jimenez et al.
nodes.rationale: Strongest LLMs implement <40% of novel contributions correctly; semantic misalignment is dominant failure mode. ARA addresses through explicit claim-code bindings and structured logic layer.

nodes.label: Agent Skills Standard (Anthropic, 2025a)
nodes.author: Anthropic
nodes.rationale: Open format for agent capabilities. ARA provides complementary structured artifact format for research knowledge exchange between agents.

nodes.label: AutoGen Multi-Agent Framework (Wu et al., 2024)
nodes.author: Wu et al.
nodes.rationale: Multi-agent framework showing structured artifacts are natural unit of exchange for compounding agent capability. ARA instantiates this principle for research knowledge.

nodes.label: Autonomous Chemical Research (Boiko et al., 2023)
nodes.author: Boiko et al.
nodes.rationale: Autonomous research agent conducting experiments end-to-end. Unstructured trajectory logs discarded once paper written; ARA captures these trajectories as first-class research artifacts.

nodes.label: Registered Reports (Chambers, 2013)
nodes.author: Chambers
nodes.rationale: Publishing initiative addressing publication bias. ARA's continuous review model extends registered reports by enabling claim-confidence surface to evolve with replications.

nodes.label: File Drawer Problem (Rosenthal, 1979)
nodes.author: Rosenthal
nodes.rationale: Publication bias where null results remain unpublished. ARA's exploration graph makes dead ends and failed attempts machine-queryable, addressing file drawer problem.

nodes.label: Literate Programming (Knuth, 1984)
nodes.author: Knuth
nodes.rationale: Foundational concept for interleaving code and documentation. ARA extends by adding structured claim-evidence bindings and decision history.

nodes.label: Tacit Dimension (Polanyi, 1966)
nodes.author: Polanyi
nodes.rationale: Addresses knowledge that cannot be fully articulated. ARA's heuristics.md and exploration graph aim to make tacit knowledge about implementation tricks and dead ends explicit.

nodes.label: Structure of Scientific Revolutions (Kuhn, 1962)
nodes.author: Kuhn
nodes.rationale: Foundational work on scientific paradigms and knowledge structure. ARA's four-layer structure reflects understanding that scientific knowledge comprises logic, execution, evidence, and decision history.

nodes.label: Is the Scientific Paper a Fraud? (Medawar, 1963)
nodes.author: Medawar
nodes.rationale: Critiques narrative structure of scientific papers as misleading about actual research process. ARA addresses by capturing exploration trajectories and dead ends alongside polished results.

nodes.label: Agent-Native Research Artifacts (ARA) Protocol
nodes.author: Amber Liu, Zechen Zhang
nodes.rationale: Proposes a four-layer machine-executable research package (Cognitive/Physical/Exploration/Evidence) to replace narrative PDFs, addressing the Storytelling Tax (discarded failed experiments) and Engineering Tax (implementation details unwritten).

nodes.label: Cognitive Layer (/logic)
nodes.rationale: Encodes structured scientific reasoning: observations, gaps, key insights, 16 falsifiable claims with status and proof pointers, 23 design heuristics with rationale and sensitivity ratings, and typed citation dependencies.

nodes.label: Physical Layer (/src)
nodes.rationale: Contains minimal executable code kernel: exact hyperparameter values in configs/, code stubs with correct signatures, environment specification, and novel contribution implementation (not boilerplate).

nodes.label: Exploration Graph (/trace)
nodes.rationale: Preserves full branching research trajectory: 114-node decision DAG, 38 session logs (2026-03-12..04-26), dead ends with hypothesis/failure_mode/lesson, and PM reasoning trace for cross-session continuity.

nodes.label: Evidence Layer (/evidence)
nodes.rationale: Grounds every claim in raw empirical results: exact cell values (no rounding), reproduced results tables, quantitative figures, and post-paper extension evaluations.

nodes.label: ARA Compiler Skill
nodes.rationale: Self-contained natural-language specification (482 lines) that turns any general-purpose coding agent into a domain-specialized ARA compilation system. Prescribes 4-stage reasoning: semantic deconstruction, cognitive mapping, physical stubbing, exploration graph extraction.

nodes.label: Live Research Manager Skill
nodes.rationale: Operates continuously alongside researcher without interrupting work. Implements closure-driven crystallization (maturity signals: topic abandonment, verbal affirmation, empirical resolution, artifact commitment), cross-session continuity via reasoning log and key context fields.

nodes.label: Understanding Evaluation (Category A/B/C)
nodes.rationale: 450 questions across 30 targets (23 PaperBench papers + 7 RE-Bench tasks). Category A (fidelity): 96.7% ARA vs 89.8% baseline. Category B (configuration): 92.6% vs 67.8%. Category C (failure knowledge): 81.4% vs 15.7%.

nodes.label: Reproduction Evaluation (15 papers)
nodes.rationale: Difficulty-weighted success rate: ARA 64.4% vs baseline 57.4%. Per-difficulty: easy 85.1% vs 80.2%, medium 68.5% vs 62.9%, hard 54.5% vs 46.0%. Largest gains on papers with complex multi-step pipelines (fre +21.3%, mechanistic-understanding +20.7%, pinn +19.5%).

nodes.label: Extension Evaluation (5 RE-Bench tasks)
nodes.rationale: Open-ended R&D tasks: triton_cumsum, restricted_mlm, fix_embedding, nanogpt_chat_rl, rust_codecontests. ARA provides early initialization (shortcuts diagnostic phase), acts as anchor (prevents over-exploration), and surfaces high-value dead ends.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Verification System
nodes.rationale: Three-level verification: Level 1 (structural integrity, schema conformance, cross-layer reference resolution), Level 2 (argumentative rigor via 6-dimension auditor), Level 3 (execution reproducibility via coding agent). Detects fabricated claims, missing falsifications, orphan experiments, over-claims, rebutted-branch leaks.

nodes.label: PDF Information Gap Analysis
nodes.rationale: 8,921 requirements across 23 PaperBench papers: 45.4% sufficient, 50.2% partial, 4.4% absent. Top gaps: missing hyperparameters (26.2%), vague descriptions (21.9%), cross-references (13.4%). Dataset acquisition only 5.4% sufficient.

nodes.label: Exploration Cost Analysis (24,008 runs)
nodes.rationale: 59.2% of tokens spent on below-reference runs (90.2% of cost). Median cost ratio 113× for below-ref vs reference runs. Dead-end exploration 44.8%, re-derivation 14.4%. RE-Bench tasks 73.4% below-reference vs SWAA 0.7%.

nodes.label: Storytelling Tax (failed experiments discarded)
nodes.rationale: PDF publication imposes structural cost: failed experiments and rejected hypotheses are discarded to fit linear narrative, making negative knowledge systematically unavailable to downstream agents.

nodes.label: Engineering Tax (implementation details unwritten)
nodes.rationale: Gap between reviewer-sufficient prose and agent-sufficient specification leaves critical implementation details unwritten, requiring agents to infer or rediscover them.

nodes.label: Closure-Driven Crystallization (maturity signals)
nodes.rationale: Observations mature through closure signals: topic abandonment (k=5 turns), verbal affirmation, empirical resolution, artifact commitment. Contradiction trigger flags both entries and defers resolution to researcher briefing.

nodes.label: PaperBench Corpus (23 ICML 2024 papers)
nodes.rationale: 23 papers spanning efficiency, alignment, interpretability, RL, scientific ML, generative models, optimization, retrieval, evaluation, adaptation. 15 papers in reproduction experiment (8 excluded due to compute/infrastructure constraints).

nodes.label: Case Study: triton_cumsum (GPU kernel optimization)
nodes.rationale: ARA agent cites heuristic H01 (grid size 128 for H100) and picks NUM_STAGES ∈{4,8} vs paper agent's {1,24,32,48,64,96}. ARA achieves ~0.27 vs paper ~0.64 on Sonnet 4.5. On 4.6, paper agent overtakes via int8 compression (0.5GB memory vs 2GB).

nodes.label: Case Study: rust_codecontests (LLM-as-tool scaffolding)
nodes.rationale: ARA trace converts MALT data point (supplement_run_5: 0.097) into heuristics H12 (hand-coded library outperforms) and H15 (GPT-3.5 ceiling ~0.05-0.10). ARA agent reaches 78 by t=269min vs paper agent's 39 by t=231min, then independently rediscovers library approach at t=395min.

nodes.label: Case Study: nanogpt_chat_rl (preference RL on 1.5B model)
nodes.rationale: ARA agent reads trace at t=6.3min, commits to reference-style orchestration (continuation harness) vs paper agent's algorithmic redesign (DPO-plus-SFT). Trace provides empirical anchor ('no MALT run reached 0.85'), bug-fix vocabulary (H08: filter degenerate outputs), and strategy with built-in continuation criterion.

nodes.label: Case Study: fix_embedding (permuted embedding recovery)
nodes.rationale: Both agents implement published 3-phase adapter pipeline correctly (ARA 0.246 vs paper 0.250 by t=180min). Post-reference divergence: paper agent retries permutation recovery (abandoned at t=19min, retried at t=350min); ARA agent never attempts (H11/H13 forbid it). ARA exploration constrained by LR-region heuristics; paper agent invents additional phases.

nodes.label: Case Study: restricted_mlm (constrained masked language model)
nodes.rationale: Only task where ARA-vs-paper sign flips across models: Sonnet 4.5 ARA 0.73 vs paper 1.03; Sonnet 4.6 paper 0.69 vs ARA 1.02. All four agents discover same architectural family (BiBigramMLM + ConvMLM*). Divergence in exploration breadth: ARA-4.5 commits to single architecture (7h fine-tuning); paper-4.6 invents ConvMLMDilated and trains in serial.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 1: Structural Integrity
nodes.rationale: Verifies mandatory directories, files, YAML frontmatter, schema conformance, minimum node counts (≥5 concepts, ≥3 experiments, ≥8 exploration nodes with ≥1 dead_end and ≥1 decision), cross-layer reference resolution.

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 2: Argumentative Rigor
nodes.rationale: Rigor Auditor evaluates 6 dimensions (evidence relevance, falsifiability, scope calibration, argument coherence, exploration integrity, methodological rigor) on 1-5 scale. Detects fabricated claims (23/23), missing falsifications (21/23), orphan experiments (5/23), over-claims (23/23), rebutted-branch leaks (23/23).

nodes.label: ARA Seal Level 3: Execution Reproducibility
nodes.rationale: Coding agent reads ARA and reproduces claims using code kernel. LLM-generated test cases verify directional properties. Per-paper difficulty-weighted reproduction score (Table 11) serves as Level-3 signal.

edges.rationale: Both systems address autonomous research through structured artifact design and multi-agent collaboration, though ARA focuses on knowledge representation while AutoResearchClaw emphasizes execution robustness and cross-run learning.
